solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A measure of work in a lot of organs

parts.note: a lot of things means many of them
ears are the organs of hearing

explanation.surface: A statistic about how much labour is involved in building or playing many church organs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organs' suggests pipe organs, but here they are body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-years is a unit for the labour of one person working through a whole year.

clue.text: Has a try to repair saucer

indicators.note: to repair something is to put it back together, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to mend a broken saucer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' makes HASATRY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish for cigarette ash is a kind of saucer, so the specific item is defined by its general type.

clue.text: Lose years, dreadfully idle

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lazy person wastes years of their life by being dreadfully idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose' looks like part of the surface story, but it is the definition: to yield ground is to lose it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield ground is to give it up or concede it, so the verb can mean lose.

clue.text: Part of Joan's circle?

parts.note: Joan is the French heroine of Orleans, and the word after 'Joan of' in her name is also the term for a portion of a circle's circumference

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joan's circle' sounds like her friends, but it is the word that follows 'Joan of'; that word is also a portion of a circle's circumference.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved section of a circle's circumference is geometrically called by this word, which is also Joan of ___'s surname.

clue.text: Pretended to be encouraged, wasting time

indicators.note: wasting time means losing it, so a T is dropped from the word

parts.note: to be stimulated is to be spurred on or encouraged

explanation.surface: Someone faked being motivated while really just idling time away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from STIMULATED ('wasting time').
explanation.definitionFit: Simulated means faked or feigned, so it is a synonym of pretended.

clue.text: Really great to embrace peace at last

parts.note: to embrace someone is to hug them

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of peace

explanation.surface: It is wonderful finally to be able to make peace with a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge means enormous, so it is a synonym of very great in size.

clue.text: Ugly skin, old, on us

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A grumble that ageing has left our skin looking unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means extremely unattractive, a stronger synonym of ugly.

clue.text: Allow George at first to sound off

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of George

parts.note: to sound off is to rant, holding forth angrily

explanation.surface: Letting a man named George be the first to air his grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a request is to permit it, so the verb is a synonym of allow.

clue.text: Out of order, so he put a sock in it!

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing a sock is put into

indicators.note: out of order means not in its proper sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man who is behaving badly to be quiet: 'put a sock in it!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a sock in it!' is slang for 'shut up', but read literally it describes footwear, which you put on over a sock.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is what you pull on over a sock, so the item is cryptically defined as where a sock goes.

clue.text: Fellow broadcasters with new entertainer

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-worker
the media are the broadcasters and press collectively

explanation.surface: A man joins some broadcasters along with a new performer.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the prefix meaning fellow (co-pilot, co-author).
explanation.definitionFit: A comic who tells jokes on stage is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Remind one young lady to be lavish

parts.note: to prod someone is to nudge or remind them
I is the Roman numeral for one
gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A warning to a young woman not to be extravagant.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, which is one sense of lavish.

clue.text: Berliner for one rejected colourful herb

parts.note: a person from Berlin is an example of a German

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour, so taken as an example of colourful

explanation.surface: A man from Berlin turns down a brightly coloured herb.
explanation.walkthrough: A Berliner is also a doughnut, but here it is a person from Berlin, an example of a German; 'colourful' stands for one colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a plant of the mint family, Teucrium, grown as an aromatic garden plant.

clue.text: Farm animals head off for crop

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: goats are animals kept on farms

explanation.surface: Farm livestock wandering off to graze on a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the G from GOATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain grown in fields, an example of an arable crop.

clue.text: Pearl here maybe made up story about English

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the E
a made-up story is invented, and made up here means the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A fabricated tale about a pearl, perhaps told by an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' turns STORY into OYSTR, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls form inside shellfish, so this mollusc is where a pearl may be found.

clue.text: Everything British in miniature chest of drawers

indicators.note: in means the following letters are placed inside

parts.note: a toy version of something is a miniature one, as in a toy poodle
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything British fits inside a tiny chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall piece of bedroom furniture, a double chest with drawers stacked high.

clue.text: Knock it back — healthy drink

indicators.note: knock it back reads as downing a drink, but knock back here means send the word back, reading it in reverse
back completes the instruction to turn the word round

parts.note: sane means sound of mind, healthy in mind

explanation.surface: Telling someone to down a health drink in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock it back' sounds like drinking quickly, but it says to reverse IT, giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal infusion, a type of tea, so it is something to drink.

clue.text: Cooking hot flan? Absolutely!

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked if they want a hot flan being cooked, and agrees enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation is ironic understatement used for emphatic agreement, like saying certainly.

clue.text: The cheek of judge, a wise old bird

parts.note: the owl is traditionally the wise old bird

explanation.surface: Indignation at the insolence of a judge who is a wise old character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' suggests impudence, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A jowl is the lower part of the face along the jaw, the flesh of the cheek.

clue.text: One broadcasting is walking here with delight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a presenter currently transmitting is said to be live on the radio or TV
second meaning: to be overjoyed is to be 'walking on' this, an idiom for elation

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one phrase: the broadcasting term, and the idiom 'walking on ___' for being blissfully happy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a programme being transmitted live, and completes the idiom for elation about walking.

clue.text: Showing rashness, I must abandon car at a big town

indicators.note: must abandon means the I has to be left out of the word

parts.note: Audi is a make of car
a city is a big town

explanation.surface: A reckless driver is forced to leave the car behind in a large town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I must abandon car' takes I out of AUDI, leaving AUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity means bold daring that ignores risk, close in sense to recklessness.

clue.text: Subdued, being married together

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning together or jointly, as in cooperate
to be married is to be wed

explanation.surface: A couple who have been married a long time have become quiet and tamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowed means intimidated into submission, a synonym of subdued.

clue.text: Pointed remarks about a party island

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: barbs are cutting or pointed remarks
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Cutting comments about a party held on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean island nation in the West Indies.

clue.text: Small coin not quite enough for broth

indicators.note: not quite enough means just short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: A small coin is too little to pay for a bowl of broth.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou was an old French coin of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was an old French coin worth very little, hence a tiny sum.

clue.text: Feeble few days broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting is sending out sound, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a week is a few days

explanation.surface: A frail effort after a short spell on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak means lacking strength, so it is a synonym of feeble.

clue.text: Earnestly request quiet bit of sunshine

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
a ray is a single beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: Someone asks quietly for a little sunny weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to beg or beseech, an earnest plea.

clue.text: Finish tidily, part of competition being cancelled

parts.note: a round is one stage of a competition
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A stage of a tournament is called off, which neatly concludes matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To round off is to complete something neatly with a fitting final touch.
